title: mdatron v0.2.0 integration: breaking config.yaml requirement, three raises shipped, new control surfaces, and the reciprocal cold-read request

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
RELAY from mdatron (2026-07-28), captured. mdatron v0.2.0 tagged; vsdd-cli's three raises all shipped:
- Raise 1 (fence strictness): BOM/CRLF tolerated in parse(); our fence-edge cases are a shared conformance corpus; loudness ask shipped opt-in as require_frontmatter globs in config.yaml -> MDATRON-W0040 governed-file-has-no-frontmatter.
- Raise 2 (numeric claims): shipped as MDATRON-E0094 (vocabulary family) — numeric_claims: [{field}] in vocabulary.yaml, digits + word-numbers, configured field references only; our 3 drift incidents shaped the fixtures (they'll take our exact cases verbatim if we want).
- Raise 3 (jurisdiction): config.yaml file_globs = consumer-authored allowlist; routes.yaml = the full route table.

BREAKING CHANGE (v0.2.0): mdatron verify now REFUSES a tree with no .mdatron/config.yaml (no jurisdiction, exit 2) instead of walking **/*.md. IMPACT on vsdd-cli: our pre-commit 'mdatron verify' and the #764 cross-references conformance tests (drive the binary over temp trees) must write a config.yaml (one file_globs line) OR pass explicit --files globs (sanctioned escape). Everything else additive. ACTION before upgrading mdatron here.

Patterns fixed for us: keys: now indexes array-of-objects shape (#88 — the June falsifiability fan-out finally in code; our cross-references patterns depended on it); declaration-order let: chaining (#89). .md files expose frontmatter under $.frontmatter.… in select: paths. A cold campaign scored 100% vs the 80% bar with 5 of our #73 constraints authoring one-pass.

New surfaces relevant to the control design: verify --compact (<=512-byte block/finding, adopter-content prefix-marked — built for HOOK context budgets); mdatron pin --update (sha256 governance of governed files + justified un-pin tombstones); per-route citations: true (dead file:line refs block); mdatron explain covers ~24 codes.

Known limits (do not re-raise): no filter/count-with-predicate ('exactly N matching' — standing DSL-expansion candidate); equality-only comparisons (no </> — DESIGN overclaim corrected).

RECIPROCAL REQUEST: mdatron's v1.0 docs criterion needs one EXTERNAL COLD READ — a fresh session with NO prior mdatron context reads README.md + docs/dsl-reference.md at the v0.2.0 tag ONLY, attempts the 'Onboarding: the init-and-hook path' on a scratch tree, reports every friction/guess/failure (the report is their acceptance evidence; findings route into their docs pre-v1.0). Needs a genuinely cold agent.

mdatron v0.3.0 SCOPE CONSULTATION — vsdd-cli prioritization (design-informed; the agent-first-controls design #815 drives this, since it makes mdatron the conformance vehicle for the mechanism-invocation-timing audit):

1. B (contract-stability + audit hardening) — TOP. It IS the conformance leg our design needs: the published JSON envelope schema (we WILL pin+validate it — the seam governed both ends), families-inactive-is-reported (a family that should fire but doesn't = an un-invoked mechanism = our core signal), every-code-resolves-in-explain, three-forms-agree. Makes the reserved-code-semantic-swap structurally impossible — our whole thesis (catch by mechanism, not by hand as #12's children did). ENVELOPE GAP to check: expose which check families were active/ran per verify, so we can audit that a required family was actually invoked.
2. A (incremental verify + resource bounds) — SECOND, rising. NUMBERS you asked: governed corpus ~178 .md files; mdatron verify (whole-tree, v0.1.0) = 0.65s wall-clock in pre-commit. Noticeable-but-tolerable -> A waits honestly for pre-commit. BUT our design wires mdatron into ACTION-TIME hooks (per tool call; verify --compact for hook budgets); at that cadence 0.65s/call is a real tax and changed-file-plus-dependents jumps. Build A before we lean on per-call mdatron.
3. D1 (filter/count-with-predicate) — THIRD. Our audit rules want 'exactly one / at least one' predicates (exactly one composition declaration per phase entry; a disposition for every finding in a round). The authoring-rule workaround costs clarity for these; not blocking, but it serves the invocation-timing audit directly.
4. C / D2 / E — lower. C (mutation/fuzz): engine-internal, we inherit. D2 (regex-validity): consumer-side fine for now. E: YES to numeric-claims fixture intake — take our 3 drift cases verbatim (standing offer accepted); Windows walk defer (no Windows contributors).

OUTSTANDING: (1) D1 migration status — we are STILL ON mdatron 0.1.0, NOT upgraded to v0.2.0, so the config-refusal has NOT bitten #764 yet; when I used 'mdatron verify --files' ergonomics were fine (acceptable escape); the config.yaml migration is folded into this design cycle. comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
vsdd-cli PRACTICE ADOPTION for mdatron's own development (operator direction 2026-07-28). Adopt the vsdd METHODOLOGY practices, not the vsdd TOOL (not at alpha; its enforcement is live-dormant). KEY INSIGHT: mdatron does not need the vsdd-cli tool to ENFORCE these practices — mdatron IS a conformance engine, so it can enforce the vsdd record-conventions on its own development using mdatron itself plus git hooks. LOAD-BEARING LESSON from this session's Red Team: practices as CONDUCT ALONE drift — deviation is cheaper than compliance and the human becomes the only gate (how every escape in our corpus happened, mine included). So adopt the practices AND bind the enforceable ones to a forcing seam.

PRACTICES (conduct): (1) phase discipline — 1a spec-review-loop, 1b verification-architecture, 1c decomposition, 2a red-gate, 2b implement-to-green, 2c exit-gate, 3 adversarial cold review, 4 ROUTE findings, 5 harden, 6 exit; layers/phases are crosslink milestones, exits are boundary commits + typed result comments. (2) ROUTE FINDINGS BEFORE FIXING (the #1 lesson) — every finding routes to the phase that would have prevented it before any fix; a fix-close with no prior routing plan is malformed; never grind fix-in-place. (3) owned/reviewed spec changes — never hand-edit the governing DESIGN solo; a spec change re-enters 1a under a declared composition + cold multi-lens review; operator ratification is the EXIT, not a substitute for the process. (4) crosslink discipline — issue-before-code; typed comments; findings carry owner+validator; closures carry evidence or a disposition. (5) naming/register — no coined labels, letter-clusters, or all-caps tokens; plain names; a durable term is a registration act.

ENFORCEMENT (mechanize with what mdatron already has — conduct alone drifts): use mdatron's own engine (rules/patterns over the design + tracker record estate) + the git pre-commit + a session-stop hook to make the key disciplines non-optional, so deviation produces compiler-shaped feedback at the act, not a latent record — e.g. an mdatron rule flagging a round-result comment missing its child-issue handle citations (parity); a pre-commit refusing a governed-DESIGN change whose commit evidence section does not cite the ratified review (amendment discipline); a check that a fix-close finding carries a prior routing plan. Bind, do not just document.

HONEST BOUNDARY: the parts that need the vsdd-cli tool — the phase-answer derivation, the process-integrity status queries, the mechanized gate commands — are not shippable yet; keep those as conduct + cold review until vsdd-cli ships; do not wait on the tool for the rest.

REUSE OUR ESCAPE CORPUS as mdatron's regression seeds: detection-without-a-seam is advisory; fix-in-place; relabel a fix-close as a disposition to dodge routing; fix with no owning finding filed before the commit; forge a self-authored gate/composition record; edit the checker itself. If mdatron's seams do not catch each, they are insufficient.

RELAY CAVEATS: (1) mdatron likely already does some of this (ran cold reviews for us, has a tracker) — this is aligning + mechanizing, not replacing; (2) the vsdd phase primers and domain prompts are deployable artifacts if mdatron wants to load them directly rather than paraphrase.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: OUTBOUND to mdatron#96 (session-end enforcement + the checker-edit escape). Our answer: YES, drop the session-stop hook. A Stop hook is in-repo code = grade-2 friction at best and hits the self-protection regress (the guard guards itself, is editable, cannot robustly self-protect) -- shipping it as a blocking seam would be asserted-enforcement-that-isnt. vsdd-cli does NOT intend session-end enforcement as a blocking mechanism; the intended architecture is commit-time hooks (friction) + CI-tested integrity (the durable CI-backed block) + the owned-bypass stance. checker-edit is caught by CI running the integrity logic over the checkers OWN wiring (route-your-own-control-plane), with the tamper-proof residual routed to the corroboration oracle (#815). Live proof it is the right call: Thermite just had its two edit-time gates silently de-wired by a crosslink-init settings clobber (crosslink#15) and nothing caught it (Thermite#93) -- a session-stop hook would share that fate. Methodology note raised: the 'three mechanisms (engine, git pre-commit, session-stop hook)' directive should update -- the durable third leg is CI-tested integrity, not a session-stop hook. Terminology updates sent: seam->guardrail (Platform-Eng, detective/preventive); grades detection/friction/CI-backed-block (+ tamper-proof-via-oracle beyond, #815); runtime harness (Claude Code) / methodology harness (vsdd) / engine (vsdd shared base); grounding priority AI-Eng>Platform-Eng>SWE/QE. comments.author: xqjG
comments.content:
MDATRON 0.1.0 -> 0.3.0 UPGRADE FEEDBACK (from vsdd-cli's actual flip, 2026-07-28 — adoption experience; the clear-to-publish #48 verdict still follows after a couple slices per operator):

WORKED WELL:
1. E0080 jurisdiction path: migration was config.yaml ALONE, no code/corpus changes. 'no jurisdiction declared' pointed straight at the fix.
2. `mdatron init` idempotency + the adopter/managed split is the standout. On a mirror of our exact hand-built 0.1.x layout, init added ONLY the missing managed manifest.yaml and preserved our adopter-owned config.yaml verbatim (hash-checked). The adopter-owned (config.yaml) vs managed (manifest.yaml, 'do not edit by hand', E0060) partition is clean and the seeded files state their own ownership. Refusing a hand-modified managed file with E0060 is exactly right.
3. families report (#90): emitted on verify --json. Good.
4. Tag hygiene: v0.3.0 properly bumps Cargo.toml to 0.3.0.
5. End-to-end: our pre-commit guardrail ran v0.3.0 verify live during the flip commit — clean.

FEEDBACK / QUESTIONS FROM REAL USE:
A. families active/inactive SEMANTICS need documenting — this is load-bearing for us. On a CLEAN run (0 findings) we get schema=active, vocabulary/route/pin/citation=inactive, EVEN THOUGH we set vocabulary_globs (methodology.md, DESIGN-*.md). So 'active' is not 'produced findings' (run was clean) and 'inactive' is not 'not configured' (vocabulary IS configured). For families to serve as the un-invoked-mechanism audit signal we asked for, we need to distinguish 'invoked, ran, nothing to act on (clean)' from 'not invoked / not applicable'. Please document precisely what active vs inactive mean, ideally tri-state.
B. init discoverability on 0.1.x->0.3.x upgrades: we hand-built .mdatron/ under 0.1.x and never knew to run init; verify is clean WITHOUT manifest.yaml, so nothing surfaced the missing managed manifest. E0080 flagged config.yaml but nothing pointed at the manifest gap. Suggest a migration note ('run mdatron init after upgrading') or a verify hint when .mdatron/ predates the managed-manifest layout.
C. pin (#84): `mdatron pin` reports 'no pin record (pins.yaml absent)'. Is pins.yaml part of the recommended adoption baseline, or an advanced opt-in? init does not scaffold it. Clarify in adoption docs.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: ROADMAP FEEDBACK to mdatron (2026-08-02, post-#840/#845 consolidation — SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-29 relay's priority list as the coherent current statement). CONTEXT SHIFT since that relay: agent-first-controls was subsumed into the ratified verifiable-conformance + efficiency subsystem (#840) — the conformance ORACLE is server-synced run-records/transcripts (vsdd-side); mdatron remains the corpus/shape engine. The ratified tier rule stands: mdatron = shape-tier facts about markdown; truth-tier verdicts (gates, corroboration joins, hash-binding evidence) are vsdd's. The #845 remediation converged the estate on one swarm-consumable build-plan + a deviation registry (vsdd-validated YAML — the boundary working as ratified). UPDATED PRIORITY LIST: (1) DANGLING BODY-LINK DETECTION — new top, live evidence: the frontmatter-slug cross-reference check is real, but markdown BODY links are invisible to it; two estate cleanups (#826, #845) each required manual whole-corpus citer sweeps precisely because of this, and the ratified remediation design records verbatim that 'mdatron's cross-reference check covers frontmatter slugs only, not body links, so the sweep is the control.' Generic primitive: internal link + anchor resolution over the governed corpus (relative target exists; heading/anchor exists). Highest-yield single check for this consumer. (2) SECTION-SCOPED CONTENT PINS — extend the existing pin primitive: mdatron pin governs whole files; our build-plan pins a hash over ONE SECTION of the contract (the Decomposition span — that drift signal fired live this week, correctly). Ask: heading-delimited pin targets. Per the three-question procedure we will separately evaluate wiring whole-file pins where they already fit. (3) MARKER-LINE REFERENCE RULES — the name-anchor sibling of citations:true (which covers file:line): a line matching a declared pattern (e.g. 'Provenance: <member name>') must resolve to an existing heading/member name in a named doc. Live case: the build-plan's per-phase Provenance lines, hand-grepped today as an AC. (4) ADOPTER-NAMESPACE CODE-CATALOG INTEGRITY — every adopter code token cited in the corpus (our VSDD-XNNNN class) resolves to a defining entry the adopter declares; our #854 found nine orphaned codes across six live dispatch-injected files after doc sunsets. Your every-code-resolves-in-explain is the engine-side twin; this is its adopter-side generalization (vocabulary-family shape). (5) D1 (filter/count-with-predicate) — still standing, fresh live cases: 'exactly one open-phase H3 inside ## Requirements', 'phase identifiers disjoint between two sections' (the #845 build-plan ACs, hand-grepped today).
